title: Airline refunds for canceled or significantly changed flights
facts: Under U.S. Department of Transportation rules, airline passengers are entitled to a refund when an airline cancels a flight or makes a significant change and the passenger chooses not to accept the alternative transportation or travel credit offered.
Refund obligations cover the ticket price and applicable unused ancillary-service fees under federal rules.
A passenger who accepts rebooking or travels on the changed itinerary generally does not also receive a refund for the transportation already used.
DOT rules define circumstances that constitute significant changes for refund purposes.
